sources.title: Qwen-VL official repository
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. News dates Qwen-VL-Max introduction to January 18, 2024. The README distinguishes Max from the August 2023 Qwen-VL/Qwen-VL-Chat checkpoints, whose Qwen-7B/ViT specification does not identify Max. It supplies no Max parameter count or named sized-base relationship.

sources.title: Introducing Qwen-VL
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The January 25, 2024 launch describes Plus and Max as enhanced Qwen-VL-family versions, with better visual reasoning, high-resolution recognition, text extraction and localization. It does not identify either as a variant of a named sized checkpoint or publish total/active counts.

sources.title: qwen-vl-max model card
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27, 2026 through the official search-indexed card; direct opening timed out. It still maps qwen-vl-max to qwen-vl-max-2025-08-13 and lists 131072 context tokens, text/image/video inputs, text output, and unsupported Function Calling. No nominal parameter count, active count, or named sized-base lineage appears in the indexed card.

sources.title: [Model Studio] Update of Qwen VL-Max
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The May 26, 2025 notice schedules the qwen-vl-max alias update to qwen-vl-max-2025-04-08 on June 4, 2025. This establishes a changed backing snapshot, not parameter preservation from the 2024 model or an April 8, 2024 launch.

sources.title: Structured output supported models
sources.evidence: Lists Qwen-VL-Max among non-thinking-mode visual models supporting JSON Object output, with latest/snapshot variants excluded from that particular feature listing.

sources.title: Deep thinking
sources.evidence: Documents dedicated thinking models and reasoning_content; its supported-model list does not include qwen-vl-max. General visual reasoning ability is distinct from this API mode.

sources.title: Qwen-VL-Max model page
sources.evidence: Search-indexed page shows Function Calling as a feature, conflicting with the explicit unsupported cells in the Alibaba model card. Direct open returned 404; do not treat this stale feature list as a successful current API test.

sources.title: Qwen2-VL: To See the World More Clearly
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026. The August 29, 2024 launch explicitly names Qwen2-VL-72B as its largest model and shows its official API call using model="qwen-vl-max-0809". This directly supports the historical snapshot as the nominal 72B Qwen2-VL model, not merely family resemblance. The architecture section describes Qwen2 language models with an approximately 600M-parameter ViT, image/video input, dynamic resolution and M-RoPE. The dated API mapping does not identify the later 2025-08-13 snapshot.

sources.title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model’s Perception of the World at Any Resolution
sources.evidence: Opened September 18, 2024 report on October 27, 2026. It gives nominal Qwen2-VL scales of 2B, 8B and 72B. Table 1 separately lists a 72B language model and 675M vision encoder for Qwen2-VL-72B, while the prose uses 72B as the nominal full-model scale. These are useful historical specifications, not an exact 72.675B tensor census. They do not establish component counts or activation behavior for the later Max snapshots.

sources.title: Qwen-VL-Max and Qwen-VL-Plus model update notice
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026. The September 3, 2025 notice explicitly maps stable qwen-vl-max from qwen-vl-max-2025-04-08 to qwen-vl-max-2025-08-13, effective September 16 in Beijing and Singapore. It discloses alias/version and pricing changes, but no parameter counts or relationship to a named sized base model.

sources.title: Update of Qwen-VL-Max-Latest
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026. The August 13, 2025 announcement introduces qwen-vl-max-2025-08-13 and moves the latest alias from the April 8 snapshot to it. It reports context and pricing but no total/active counts, architecture or named sized-base lineage.

sources.title: Introduction to model fine-tuning: image and video token calculation
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026; page updated October 21. The image-token section assigns qwen-vl-max 32x32 pixels per visual token, while QVQ and other Qwen2.5-VL models use 28x28. This documents a visual-processing distinction and prevents assuming an unchanged open Qwen2.5-VL vision path. It does not prove any particular parameter change or disclose total, active or component counts.

sources.title: When Visualizing is the First Step to Reasoning: MIRA, a Benchmark for Visual Chain-of-Thought
sources.publisher: MIRA authors / ByteDance Seed and university collaborators
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026 as a secondary lead for Qwen specifications. The November 2025 external benchmark labels Qwen-VL-Max as 325B in its experimental settings and tables, and identifies the API checkpoint as qwen-vl-max-0813. The parameter label has no supporting developer count or lineage citation in the reviewed text. It is not a Qwen developer disclosure and is not accepted as verified size evidence.

sources.title: Qwen2.5 VL! Qwen2.5 VL! Qwen2.5 VL!
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026 to check a possible newer lineage. The January 28, 2025 post introduces named Qwen2.5-VL models and describes changed vision processing, including window attention, RMSNorm and SwiGLU. The page does not mention qwen-vl-max or identify the later Max snapshot with a particular sized Qwen2.5-VL model.

name.note: Display-name punctuation is normalized; official model name is Qwen-VL-Max.

developer.note: Developed by Alibaba Qwen; served through Alibaba Cloud.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability in the developer repository. January 25 is the later blog date; the baseline April 8, 2024 date is unsupported. This dates initial Max availability, not the current rolling snapshot.

open_weights.note: Hosted Max is distinct from the released Qwen-VL/Qwen-VL-Chat weights. Official Max links lead to demos and API access.

license.note: No downloadable Max weight license; do not transfer the separate open checkpoint license to this hosted alias.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search found an explicit nominal 72B disclosure for the historical qwen-vl-max-0809 API snapshot through the Qwen2-VL launch; that count is retained as valid historical evidence. The subsequent alias updates establish a different 2025-08-13 backing snapshot, but no developer count or explicit relationship to a named sized base was found for that snapshot. The Qwen2-VL report separately lists its 72B LLM and 675M vision encoder; neither can be transferred across the later update without lineage evidence. An external MIRA benchmark labels Max 325B without developer attribution; that unverified claim is not promoted to a specification. The null reflects unresolved later-model identity/size, not a demand for exact checkpoint attestation or a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately from total size: the documented 2025-08-13 snapshot has no developer-published active count or sized-base lineage. The historical 72B Qwen2-VL API relationship supplies a nominal model size, not an independently reported per-token active count; its separate vision encoder also prevents treating the whole multimodal model as active on every decoded token. No active count is inferred from dense family resemblance or the later visual-token convention.

architecture.note: The historical qwen-vl-max-0809 snapshot is explicitly Qwen2-VL-72B, whose report describes a Qwen2 language model plus a ViT. The later 2025-08-13 alias has no established dense/MoE classification or named sized-base lineage. Its documented visual-token convention differs from other Qwen2.5-VL models; that distinction does not itself determine the later topology or parameter count.

context_window.note: Exact context length from the indexed official card; separate maximum input/output lengths are 129024/8192.

modalities.note: The model-specific card includes video, missing from the baseline.

reasoning.note: Means dedicated thinking/reasoning-output mode: provider classifies this alias under non-thinking visual models and omits it from thinking support. It still performs ordinary visual reasoning.

tool_call.note: Explicit model-card capability cells say unsupported; prefer these to the conflicting stale QwenCloud feature list. No live API execution was performed.

description.value: Hosted Qwen vision-language model for image, document, chart, and video understanding with text output.
description.note: Names supported tasks without implying native tool calling. Alias capabilities can change with its backing snapshot.

patch.description: Hosted Qwen vision-language model for image, document, chart, and video understanding with text output.
patch.notes: Hosted rolling alias documented as qwen-vl-max-2025-08-13. The historical qwen-vl-max-0809 API was explicitly Qwen2-VL-72B (nominal size); later snapshot size, active count and dense/MoE topology remain undisclosed. Initial Max availability: 2024-01-18. The official card says native Function Calling is unsupported.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null patches for the later alias total and active counts, while correcting the evidence gap: the August 2024 developer launch directly identifies qwen-vl-max-0809 with nominal Qwen2-VL-72B. Reopened launch sources and added the Qwen2-VL report, 2025 alias-update notices, current visual-token documentation and Qwen2.5-VL release. The documented alias subsequently moved to 2025-08-13, with no published size or explicit named sized-base lineage found; changed visual processing also prevents assuming an unchanged open-model structure. An external benchmark’s unattributed 325B label remains unverified. Preserved all unrelated prior assessments and corrections.
